title: Etale local representation and null-homotopy for finite free sources
statement: Let $U$ be a scheme with small etale site $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], let $B$ be a commutative ring, let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded cochain complex of finite free $B$-modules (each $P^i$ is isomorphic to $B^{r_i}$ for some $r_i\in\mathbb N$), and let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be any cochain complex of sheaves of $\underline B$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $\underline{P}^\bullet$ for the termwise constant sheaf complex [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and $Q$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. (1) Every morphism $\varphi:Q(\underline P^\bullet)\to Q(\mathcal F^\bullet)$ in $D(U_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ is represented, after an etale covering $\{V_j\to U\}$, by chain maps $\alpha_j:\underline P^\bullet|_{V_j}\to\mathcal F^\bullet|_{V_j}$. (2) If a chain map $\alpha:\underline P^\bullet\to\mathcal F^\bullet$ has $Q(\alpha)=0$, there is an etale covering on which it is null-homotopic: on each member there are sheaf morphisms $h^i:\underline P^i\to\mathcal F^{i-1}$ satisfying $\alpha^i=d_{\mathcal F}^{i-1}h^i+h^{i+1}d_P^i$ for every $i$.

proof.text: Put E equal to the termwise constant sheaf complex of P. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-etale-acyclic-homotopy] whenever a map from E into an acyclic complex occurs. This theorem constructs one etale cover and an actual homotopy on each member.

proof.text: Use the left calculus of fractions in the homotopy category to write phi as Q(beta) followed by inverse Q(q), for beta:E -> G and a quasi-isomorphism q:F -> G. In Lean this is DerivedCategory.left_fac. The cone of q is acyclic by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. Apply step 1 to beta followed by G -> Cone(q). The resulting local homotopy says this composite vanishes in the homotopy category.

proof.text: The mapping-cone triangle is distinguished in the homotopy category, and remains so under the additive restriction functor. Exactness of Hom into this triangle gives a local homotopy-class lift of beta through q. Fullness of the homotopy quotient supplies an actual chain map alpha whose composite with restricted q is homotopic to restricted beta.

proof.text: Exact etale inverse image preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Cancel Q of restricted q, and use naturality and inverse identities of mapDerivedCategoryFactors to identify Q(alpha) with the exact conjugation formula in the statement.

source.place: Tag 08FR, lemma-local-actual, assertions (1) and (2), specialized to the ringed small etale site with coefficient sheaf the constant ring B

proof.text: For Q(alpha)=0, the right calculus of fractions gives a quasi-isomorphism q:Z -> E such that q followed by alpha is null-homotopic; the proved source-library lemma DerivedCategory.exists_quasiIso_homotopy_zero_of_Q_map_eq_zero supplies this consequence. Exactness of Hom out of the distinguished cone triangle factors alpha, up to homotopy, through E -> Cone(q). The cone is acyclic. Apply step 1 to E -> Cone(q); compose its local null-homotopies with the chain representative of Cone(q) -> F and then with the homotopy giving the factorization. This is the required local null-homotopy of alpha.
